atomic_state_contract.real_defect: The preimage two raw static mut CInt PID/count values have conflicting valid multiCPU accesses before the sigcommon lock and while different processes hold different writer locks. Raw/volatile access does not make these accesses atomic. The new state replaces that production sharing rather than passing a shared raw counter to the caller-private helper.
atomic_state_contract.representation: One naturally aligned AtomicU64, PID bit-pattern in high32 and counter bit-pattern in low32. Initial high bits u32::MAX and count0 preserve original PID=-1/count0.
atomic_state_contract.begin: Relaxed load/CAS loop resets PID and count together only when observed PID differs. Same PID preserves budget; every do_signal entry invokes it at the original pre-lock reset point even on no-diagnostic paths.
atomic_state_contract.print_order: The budget check reads low32 as CInt and compares <64; formatter runs before a fresh load/CAS increment. Increment preserves whichever PID is current after formatter callbacks/concurrency, retries on actual changed state, and wraps only low32. No pre-call ticket, global strict64 promise, new lock/IRQ/refcount/allocation or kernel publication ordering is introduced.
atomic_state_contract.memory_order: All Relaxed operations coordinate diagnostic state only. They do not claim process/pending/frame/IRQ/XSAVE synchronization. Defined atomic sharing strengthens former data-race behavior; no attempt is made to reproduce undefined concurrent C interleavings.

Safety requires initialized aligned writable caller-owned counter with no unsynchronized concurrent access; production uses the atomic wrapper. No ABI/caller-private semantics change.
